correctness.rationale: Whitworth inclusion–exclusion gives E M_m=H_m/m and conditional g_m(x)=E[max{x,(1−x)Z}], with residual (m−1)-simplex Z. Integrating the conditional maximum against Beta(1,m−1) density yields the exact covariance finite sum. g_m is convex as an average of maxima of affine functions; its piecewise linear initial region, strict inequalities g(0)>μ>g(1/m) and g(1)>μ give exactly two level crossings, so Cʹ=−m f_m(g−μ) has the sign pattern −,+,−; C(0)=C(1)=0 forces exactly one interior zero with C negative then positive. The conditional beta density yields C(1/m)<0 (m>=3), while C(1/2)=2^(1−m)((m+1)/2−H_m)>0. Exponential spacing representation Y_i=E_i/T and gamma concentration reduce the positive crossing to m²Δ(z/m)=−zH_m+(e^z−1)(1+o(1)) uniformly at z∼log log m. Bracketing at z=log log m+log log log m±ε proves the asymptotic and critical exceedance size. Independently checked exact C_3(1/3)=−1/27, C_3(1/2)=1/24, C_4(1/4)=−25/512, and 50-step rational crossover brackets m=3..15. These finite tests are not proof of uniform asymptotics.

value.rationale: The maximum spacing measures an extreme, while the number exceeding a fixed arc length is a natural random coverage and connectivity statistic. Their dependence changes sign exactly once, and the crossover occurs at a surprising double-logarithmic threshold where the expected long-gap count diverges. This is a meaningful structural link between extreme-spacing and coverage-count regimes, with finite exact covariance and universal asymptotic across all m.
